'''Eduardo Suger Cofiño''' (November 29, 1938) is a Swiss-born Guatemalan physicist, scholar, educator, and politician.<ref name=prensa>{{cite web|url=https://www.prensalibre.com/hemeroteca/adios-billetera/|title=¡Adiós billetera!|date=2015-06-03|publisher=Prensa Libre|access-date=2021-08-17|language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UmNCDgAAQBAJ&dq=%22Eduardo+Suger%22&pg=PA594|title=Political Handbook of the World 2016-2017|last=Lansford|first=Tom|publisher=CQ Press|year=2017|page=594|access-date=11 December 2017|isbn=9781506327150}}</ref><ref name=drsuger/> He is one of the founders of [[Galileo University]] in [[Guatemala City]] and of the Suger Montano Institute.<ref name=prensa/><ref name=swiss/><ref>{{cite journal|date=2019|title=Carta del presidente|trans-title=Letter from the president|url=https://colegiomontano.edu.gt/downloads/RevistaExcelenciaEmpresarial-ReportajeColegioMontano.pdf|language=es|journal=Excelencia Empresarial|volume=26|pages=22|access-date=2021-08-23}}</ref> Suger was the first Central American to receive his PhD in physics.<ref name=periodico>{{cite journal|date=2013|title=Los 51 notables|trans-title=51 notable Guatemalans|url=https://issuu.com/elperiodicoguatemala/docs/aniversario_ep_17/82|language=es|journal=El Periódico Guatemala|pages=82|access-date=2021-08-23}}</ref>

==Early life==
Suger was born in [[Zürich, Switzerland]] on 29 November 1938 to Emilio Suger, a Swiss national, and Estela Cofiño Valladares of [[Acatenango, Chimaltenango]], Guatemala.<ref name=elite>{{cite web|url=https://www.elsoca.org/pdf/documentos/macrored.pdf|title=De élites, "Pacto de Corruptos" y el control del Estado en Guatemala|last=Solano|first=Luis|date=n.d.|publisher=El Socialista Centroamericano|access-date=2021-08-23|language=es}}</ref><ref name=perfil/><ref name=swiss>{{cite web|url=https://www.swissinfo.ch/spa/un-suizo-postula-a-la-presidencia-de-guatemala/3551168|title=Un suizo postula a la presidencia de Guatemala|date=2003-10-06|publisher=Swiss Info|access-date=2021-08-17|language=es}}</ref><ref name=fundador>{{cite web|url=https://www.publinews.gt/gt/tendencias/2019/09/08/entrevista-doctor-eduardo-suger-fundador-la-universidad-galileo.html|title=Conoce al fundador y educador detrás de Universidad Galileo|last=Pérez|first=Luisa Cecilia|date=2019-09-08|publisher=Publinews|language=es|access-date=2021-08-23}}</ref> When World War II broke out, Suger's father was called up to complete his mandatory military service.<ref name=creoque/> Suger's mother spoke no German despite living in Switzerland and traveled to the Guatemalan Consulate in Germany for help returning to Guatemala.<ref name=creoque/> Shortly after she and Suger returned, she married Enrique Castañeda Rubio, an engineer and official in the Army, and had four more children.<ref name=creoque/><ref name=elite/><ref name=perfil/> Suger lived with his  maternal grandmother nearby from the time his mother remarried until his grandmother died in 1949/1950.<ref name=perfil/>

===Education===
Suger graduated from La Preparatoria and earned extra money tutoring his classmates in math.<ref name=enero15/><ref name=perfil/> He briefly studied chemistry at [[Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala]] (USAC) before deciding to study at the [[ETH Zurich|Zürich's Federal Institute of Technology]] (ETH), the same school his role model Albert Einstein attended.<ref name=perfil/><ref name=enero15>{{cite journal|date=2015|title="Hay que apoyarse sobre hombros de gigantes"|trans-title=We must rest on the shoulders of giants|url=https://issuu.com/universidadgalileo/docs/galileono.2|language=es|journal=Revista Galileo|volume=1|issue=2|pages=6–13|access-date=2021-08-23}}</ref> He lived with his strict father and stepmother while earning his BS in physics and mathematics and MS in theoretical physics.<ref name=creoque/><ref name=pressreader/> At 20, he began teaching geometry and physics, and later worked for a quantum mechanics and molecular physics lab at [[IBM Research#Laboratories##Switzerland|IBM]].<ref name=perfil/><ref name=enero15/><ref name=creoque/><ref name=pressreader/> Suger served in the [[Swiss Armed Forces|military]] before returning to Guatemala in 1964.<ref name=enero15/><ref name=military>{{cite web|url=https://www.galileo.edu/revista-galileo/2020/05/08/reconocen-al-dr-eduardo-suger-por-su-trabajo-a-favor-de-la-educacion-superior-militar/|title=Reconocen al Dr. Eduardo Suger por su trabajo a favor de la educación superior militar|date=2021|publisher=Galileo University|access-date=2021-08-23|language=es}}</ref><ref name=perfil/><ref name=inspirada/> He subsequently earned his PhD in molecular physics the [[University of Texas at Austin]] (UTA) in 1971.<ref name=creoque/><ref name=swiss/><ref name="drsuger">{{cite news|url=https://www.galileo.edu/dr-suger/|title=Dr. Suger|date=n.d.|publisher=Universidad Galileo|access-date=2018-08-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201205231713/https://www.galileo.edu/dr-suger/|archive-date=2020-12-05|language=es}}</ref><ref name=pzp>{{cite web|url=https://www.plazapublica.com.gt/content/pequenas-cosas-que-no-cuadran|title=Pequeñas cosas que no cuadran|last=Hernández|first=Oswaldo J.|date=2011-09-05|publisher=Plaza Publica|access-date=2021-08-23|language=es}}</ref> While at UTA, he was inducted into [[Sigma Xi]] science society;<ref name=swiss/><ref name=periodico/> did labwork in a molecular physics group; and was an academic assistant for a postgraduate Classical Mechanics course.<ref name=drsuger/>

==Academic career==
Suger has been teaching [[mathematical physics]] for more than 50 years in universities in four different countries.<ref name=creoque/> He taught at the Minerva and Freundenberg Institutes in Zürich; [[University of Texas at Austin|UTA]] as a PhD candidate in Texas; as a [[Visiting scholar|visiting professor]] in the Informatics and Computer Science departments at Alberto Masferrer Salvadorean University and the [[Technological University of El Salvador]]; and [[Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala|USAC]], [[Universidad Francisco Marroquín]], [[Universidad del Valle de Guatemala]], [[Universidad Mariano Gálvez]], [[Rafael Landívar University]], and his own [[Galileo University]] in [[Guatemala City]].<ref name=drsuger/><ref name=creoque/><ref name=enero15/> During the 17 years he worked at USAC, he was affiliated with the medical sciences, engineering, chemistry, pharmacy, economic science, and architecture departments and established the secondary school teaching program.<ref name=creoque/><ref name=periodico/><ref name=drsuger/> In 1977, Suger joined the faculty at UFM and taught technology, accounting, and economic science classes.<ref name=40anos/> Later that year, he proposed the creation of a computer sciences department, which would allow for more in-depth study of these fields; the program proved so popular that it was quickly converted into the Computer Science and Information Technology Institute (IICC).<ref name=40anos/><ref name=fundador/> In 1978, enrollment for the related Systems Engineering, Informatics, and Computer Sciences department opened; in 1982, this too became an institute (FISICC) and Suger was named FISICC's first [[Dean (education)|dean]].<ref name=40anos/> FISICC eventually became part of Galileo University.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.galileo.edu/fisicc/|title=Facultad de Ingeniería de Sistemas, Informática y Ciencias de la Computación|date=n.d.|publisher=Galileo University|access-date=2021-08-24|language=es}}</ref> He also founded the School of Economics and Business Administration department.<ref name=creoque/><ref name=periodico/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.prensalibre.com/hemeroteca/adios-billetera/|title=¡Adiós billetera!|date=2015-06-03|publisher=Prensa Libre|access-date=2021-08-23|language=es}}</ref><ref name=40anos>{{cite journal|date=2018|last1=Hernández|first1=Cesar|last2=Morales|first2=Miguel|title=40 años de historia e innovación technológica|trans-title=40 years of history and technological innovation|url=https://www.galileo.edu/wp-content/uploads/2014/09/Rev.Gal_.Fissic.pdf|language=es|journal=Revista Galileo|volume=2|pages=3–7|access-date=2021-08-23}}</ref> He founded and directed the Institute of Open Education (IDEA), which challenges the structure of traditional university learning, in 1994.<ref name=40anos/><ref name=drsuger/><ref name=periodico/>

In 2000, he established Galileo University, one of the first science-technology universities in Guatemala.<ref name=fundador/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://esportsbureau.com/universidad-galileo-presenta-el-primer-torneo-intercolegial-de-deportes-electronicos/|title=Universidad Galileo presenta el primer Torneo Intercolegial de Deportes Electrónicos|last=Espinosa|first=Rafael|date=2021-07-24|publisher=Esportes Bureau|language=es|access-date=2021-08-23}}</ref> It was authorized by the Council of Private Higher Education in Guatemala the same year.<ref name=creoque/> In 2019, the university, located on Dr Eduardo Suger Cofiño Street in his honor, boasted 40,000 students.<ref name=fundador/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/universidad-galileo|title=Universidad Galileo|date=n.d.|publisher=Times Higher Education|access-date=2021-08-23|language=en}}</ref><ref name=periodico/> Since its foundation, Suger has served as Galileo University's [[Rector (academia)|rector]].<!--still in this role as of March 2020--><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.prensalibre.com/economia/vida-empresarial/universidad-galileo-incorpora-la-primera-maestria-en-derecho-procesal/|title=Universidad Galileo incorpora la primera maestría en Derecho Procesal|date=2020-03-07|last=Leonardo Mendoza|first=Norvin|publisher=Prensa Libre|access-date=2021-08-23}}</ref>

===Military===
Suger has a long history of working with the military as both an educator and an engineer.<ref name=military/><ref name=periodico/> He has been commended for his work in increasing [[Armed Forces of Guatemala|military]] access to university through his Guatemalan Army Program at Galileo University.<ref name=military/><ref name=periodico/>

During the [[Guatemalan Civil War]], he was approached by [[Ministry of Defence (Guatemala)|Chief of Defense Staff]] General Marco Antonio Espinoza to engineer a computerized system that would help the government monitor revolutionaries and other dissidents.<ref name=elite/><ref name=pro/> He was made an honorary colonel for his intelligence work.<ref name=periodico/><ref name=elite/><ref name=doctoris>{{cite web|url=https://www.prensacomunitaria.org/2021/08/oscuro-pasado-de-suger-cofino-rechazan-que-csu-quiera-otorgarle-doctor-honoris-causa/|title=Oscuro pasado de Suger Cofiño: rechazan que CSU quiera otorgarle Doctor Honoris Causa|date=2021-08-23|publisher=Prensa Comunitaria|access-date=2021-08-23|language=es}}</ref> In 2021, USAC announced they intended to award Suger with a [[Honorary degree|Doctor Honoris Causa]], also for his military service.<ref name=doctoris/> A USAC student organization dedicated to honoring the memory of more than 700 students who were murdered or disappeared during the [[Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala#Repression and decline##Laugerud and Lucas García military governments|war]] pushed back.<ref name=doctoris/> They claimed that Suger's technological modernization within the military and his tracking system worsened the [[Guatemalan Civil War#Transition to elections##Casualties|human rights violations]]{{Broken anchor|date=2026-11-07|bot=User:Cewbot/log/20201008/configuration|target_link=Guatemalan Civil War#Transition to elections##Casualties|reason= }} that characterized the war.<ref name=doctoris/> This sentiment echoes ''Albedrío'' magazine, the Pro-Human Rights Action Foundation, and [[Rafael Landívar University]]'s student newspaper ''Plaza Pública'', who directly suggest he should be held accountable for his indirect influence on the violence.<ref name=pzp/><ref name=pro>{{cite web|url=http://www.derechoshumanos.net/lesahumanidad/informes/guatemala/informeREMHI-Tomo2.htm|title=INFORME REMHI Proyecto Interdiocesano de Recuperación de la Memoria Histórica (REMHI)|date=n.d.|publisher=Fundación Acción Pro Derechos Humanos|access-date=2021-08-24|language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://plazapublica.com.gt/content/suger-el-anecdotico|title=Suger, el anecdótico|date=2011-08-11|publisher=Plaza Publica|access-date=2021-08-24|language=es}}</ref><ref name=observador/> Many publications, such as ''[[InSight Crime]]'' and ''El Observador GT'', as well as academics like Jennifer Schirmer ([[Historical Clarification Commission]]) and [[Hal Brands]] ([[Paul H. Nitze School of Advanced International Studies|Johns Hopkins]]), merely refer to the intelligence systems he helped develop rather than directly by name.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://insightcrime.org/investigations/guatemala-elites-and-organized-crime-the-cicig/|title=Guatemala Elites and Organized Crime: The CICIG|last=Dudley|first=Steven|date=2016-09-01|publisher=Insight Crime|access-date=2021-08-24|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|date=2003|title=Presentación|trans-title=Presentation|url=https://elobservadorgt.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/El-Observador-Electoral-No.-4-Octubre-de-2003.pdf|language=es|journal=El Observador ELectoral|publisher=albedrío|volume=1|number=4|pages=6–7|access-date=2021-08-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Schirmer|first=Jennifer|title=The Guatemalan Military Project: A Violence Called Democracy|url={{Google books|jpH2SpzKr-sC|pages=124|plainurl=yes}}}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|date=2010-04-01|title=Crime, Violence, and the Crisis in Guatemala: A Case Study in the Erosion of the State|url=https://press.armywarcollege.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1600&context=monographs|last=Brands|first=Hal Dr.|language=en|journal=Monographs, Books, and Publications|publisher=albedrío|volume=2|number=9|pages=21|access-date=2021-08-24}}</ref>

==Political career==
Suger ran for [[President of Guatemala]] in [[2003 Guatemalan general election|2003]] ([[Authentic Integral Development]]),<ref name=creoque>{{cite web|url=https://www.galileo.edu/wp-content/uploads/2011/07/Perfil-Dr.-Eduardo-Suger-Prensa-Libre.pdf|title=Creo que|access-date=2021-08-23|date=2011|publisher=Universidad de Galileo|newspaper=Prensa Libre|language=es}}</ref> [[2007 Guatemalan general election|2007]] ([[Social Action Centre]]),<ref name=pzp/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.electionguide.org/elections/id/2049/|title=SEPT. 9, 2007|date=n.d.|publisher=International Foundation for Electoral Systems|access-date=2021-08-23|language=en}}</ref> and [[2011 Guatemalan general election|2011]] ([[Commitment, Renewal and Order|CREO]]).<ref name=swiss/><ref name=elmundo/> In 2003, he received 2.23% of the votes; in 2007, 7.45%; and in 2011, he took third place with 16.4% of the vote.<ref name=observador>{{cite journal|date=2007|title=El poder detrás de los presidenciables|trans-title=The power behind the presidential candidates|url=http://www.albedrio.org/htm/otrosdocs/comunicados/ElObservadorNo9yEl%20ObservadorElectoralNo5octubre%202007.pdf|language=es|journal=El Observador ELectoral|publisher=albedrío|volume=2|number=9|pages=14|access-date=2021-08-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=McClintock|first=Cynthia|title=Electoral Rules and Democracy in Latin America|url={{Google books|fZNODwAAQBAJ|pages=147|plainurl=yes}}}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ourcampaigns.com/CandidateDetail.html?CandidateID=162272|title=Suger, Eduardo|date=2011-08-25|publisher=Our Campaigns|access-date=2018-11-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181116085929/https://www.ourcampaigns.com/CandidateDetail.html?CandidateID=162272|archive-date=2018-11-16|language=en}}</ref> He has been criticized for only engaging in politics during campaign season, preferring instead to return to his academic career, and for not aligning himself with a political party unless they approach him to be their presidential candidate.<ref name=perfil/><ref name=pzp/>

If elected, one of Suger's main priorities would be to improve Guatemala's education system.<ref name=perfil/><ref name=swiss/> He is a critic of the complexity of public higher education and claims it often is what delays institutional changes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://agg.org.gt/blog/revista-gerencia/educacion-publica-superior-en-crisis/|title=Educación pública superior, en crisis|date=2014-08-29|publisher=AGG|access-date=2021-08-23|language=es|last=Morales Monzón|first=Carlos}}</ref> He encourages strengthening the "academic-productivity"<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.albedrio.org/htm/articulos/f/fcajas-001.htm|last=Cajas|first=Fernando|title=Lo bueno y lo malo de un debate|date=2005-07-02|publisher=Albed Rio|access-date=2021-08-23|language=es}}</ref> and believes everyone deserves an equal right to education, even [[Guerrilla warfare|guerrilla soldiers]].<ref name=pzp/> He planned to eliminate poverty by expanding the middle class and by heavily investing in and empowering those in the [[Guatemalan Civil War|war-torn]] northwestern part of the country.<ref name=swiss/><ref name=elmundo>{{cite web|url=https://www.elmundo.es/america/2011/09/02/noticias/1314985769.html|last=Arrazola|first=Carlos|title=Eduardo Suger: 'Hay que borrar la muerte por hambre y la desnutrición infantil'|date=2011-02-09|publisher=El Mundo|access-date=2021-08-23|language=es}}</ref> He was also interested in turning Guatemala's [[Unitary state|centralized]] governmental structure into a [[federal republic]] and strengthening the relationship between his home countries of Guatemala and Switzerland.<ref name=inspirada/><ref name=derechos/>

==Personal life==
In 1960, Suger met Regina Margarita Castillo Rodríguez during a visit to Guatemala while on holiday from [[ETH Zurich|ETH Zürich]].<ref name=perfil/> They continued to correspond by mail before he returned in 1964.<ref name=perfil/><ref name=inspirada>{{cite web|url=https://www.swissinfo.ch/spa/una-guatemala--inspirada-en-el-modelo-suizo-/6132038|last=Domínguez|first=Norma|title=Una Guatemala 'inspirada en el modelo suizo'|date=2007-09-07|publisher=Swiss Info|access-date=2021-08-23|language=es}}</ref><ref name=pressreader>{{cite web|url=https://www.pressreader.com/guatemala/prensa-libre/20200223/281496458311595|title=A los 82 años, Eduardo Suger sigue impulso de innovación|last=Guerra|first=Hernán|date=2020-02-23|publisher=Prensa Libre|website=Press Reader|access-date=2021-08-23|language=es}}</ref>  They married on 11 January 1964 in Guatemala.<ref name=perfil>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tematicalarevista.com/?p=796|title=DR. EDUARDO SUGER|date=December 16, 2013|website=www.tematicalarevista.com|language=es-ES|access-date=2018-11-09}}</ref> The couple has five sons: José Eduardo, Carlos Enrique, Emilio Alejandro, Christian Andree, and Jean Paul.<ref name=creoque/><ref name=perfil/><ref name=obit/> Jean Paul (Administrative Vice President), José Eduardo (Dean of FISICC), Christian (Director of Materials Distribution), and Carlos (Director of Operations) all work at Galileo.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.galileo.edu/acerca-de-galileo/autoridades-de-la-universidad/|title=Autoridades de la Universidad|date=n.d.|publisher=Galileo University|access-date=2021-08-24|language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.galileo.edu/directorio/carlos-suger/|title=Carlos Suger|date=n.d.|publisher=Galileo University|access-date=2021-08-24|language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.galileo.edu/directorio/christian-suger/|title=Christian Suger|date=n.d.|publisher=Galileo University|access-date=2021-08-24|language=es}}</ref> Regina died on 16 March 2021.<ref name=obit>{{cite web|url=https://emisorasunidas.com/2021/03/16/muere-esposa-eduardo-suger-cofino/|title=Nota de duelo: Muere esposa del doctor Eduardo Suger Cofiño|date=2021-03-16|publisher=emisoras unidas|access-date=2021-08-23|language=es}}</ref>

Suger's uncle was businessman José Cofiño Ubico, who cofounded [[Industrias Licoreras de Guatemala]].<ref name=periodico/><ref>{{cite book|last=Grimaldi|first=Luis|title=El doctor Cofiño, Vida y época|url={{Google books|5Lz1DwAAQBAJ|plainurl=yes}}}}</ref> His wife is descended from the founders of [[Cervecería Centro Americana]].<ref name=periodico/>

==Publications==
Suger published four editions (1971, 1974, 1978, 1981) of the textbook ''Introducción a la matemática moderna'', which he wrote with Bernardo Morales Figueroa and Leonel Pinot Leiva.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Suger Cofiño|first1=Eduardo|last2=Morales Figueroa|first2=Bernardo|last3=Pinot Leiva|first3=Leonel|title=Introducción a la matemática moderna|url={{Google books|n_QXPAAACAAJ|plainurl=yes}}}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last1=Suger Cofiño|first1=Eduardo|last2=Morales Figueroa|first2=Bernardo|last3=Pinot Leiva|first3=Leonel|title=Introducción a la matemática moderna|url={{Google books|HLcvnAEACAAJ|plainurl=yes}}}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last1=Suger Cofiño|first1=Eduardo|last2=Morales Figueroa|first2=Bernardo|title=Introducción a la matemática moderna|url={{Google books|EvMlxQEACAAJ|plainurl=yes}}}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=Introducción a la matemática moderna|date=n.d.|publisher=WorldCat|oclc=27817850 }}</ref>
